Summary: Trade Database (Postgres)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A normalised Postgres schema for accounts, instruments, orders and positions is designed by the team and version controlled as numbered migration files. \\ * One command takes an empty database to fully migrated and seeded, loading the provided seed files in full. \\ * An ER diagram, index justifications and the historical trade data design are committed, and every team member can walk the model unaided. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This is the platform's memory. Sprint 6 writes orders to it, Sprint 7 settles against it, Sprint 9 renders what it returns. \\ * No schema file ships in contracts/ and no starter code ships on this branch. Contracts, infrastructure, the seed files and the acceptance harness are provided; the migrations, the apply command and the design documents are yours. \\ * Fundamentals of business software development are recapped inside this sprint rather than taught from scratch. \\ * Historical trade data is delivered as a documented design in DESIGN.md, not as built tables. \\ * Definition of done includes sprint-03-trade-database/scripts/check.sh passing. \\ * Security focus: constraints enforced by the database rather than hoped for in application code, least-privilege roles for the application connection, no secrets in connection config (OWASP A03).

Summary: Conceptual Data Model & ER Diagram
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Entities, attributes and relationships for the trading domain are identified from the brief and from the seed data. \\ * One ER diagram in design/ shows every entity, its attributes, its keys, and the cardinality and optionality of every relationship. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Read the domain section of the sprint brief and seed/README.md before drawing anything; the data is a second description of the domain. \\  \\ Identify the entities and model the cardinality and optionality between them. \\  \\ Commit the diagram as Mermaid in design/er-diagram.md, or as an exported image, alongside a short data dictionary. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Mermaid is the better choice because it diffs in review and cannot drift out of the repository. \\ * Every member walks the whole diagram unaided at the review, not the part they drew.

Summary: Normalised Relational Schema (1NF to 3NF)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The schema is in third normal form with no redundant or transitive dependencies. \\ * Any deliberate denormalisation is documented in design/ with the reason for it. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Translate the ER diagram into a normalised relational design. \\  \\ Record the normalisation notes and any justified denormalisation in design/. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Third normal form is mandatory for this run and is not traded away for time.

Summary: Schema Migrations, Keys and Constraints
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The schema is created by numbered .sql files in migrations/, applied in filename order, and the database can be rebuilt from those files alone. \\ * Foreign keys and check constraints enforce the domain rules, including a unique constraint on the order idempotency key. \\ * At least three check constraints exist, one of them covering account state. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create migrations/ and number the files from 001_, three digits, so the number is the order. \\  \\ Model the three account states, the reversible suspension and the closed account that is never deleted. \\  \\ Model an instrument that has stopped trading without removing the row, so that old orders still resolve. \\  \\ Record an order when it is received and allow exactly one terminal state; there is no half-filled state. \\  \\ Enforce idempotency with a database constraint rather than a read followed by a write, because two concurrent requests both pass a read-then-write check. \\  \\ Carry a version on the account row so that the second writer of a concurrent balance update discovers that it lost. \\  \\ Choose types that represent money exactly and apply them consistently. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Editing a migration in place is fine until the first design review. After it, change the schema by adding 002_, 003_ and so on: from Sprint 6 your teammates have databases with data in them. \\ * Sprint 6 depends on the unique violation being detectable, so design for that failure now.

Summary: One-Command Apply Script
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * One command takes an existing empty database to fully migrated and seeded, without prompting. \\ * The command reads its target from TARGET_DATABASE, falling back to POSTGRES_DB from the repository .env, and exits non-zero the moment anything fails. \\ * The command is declared in manifest.env as APPLY_COMMAND and runs from the sprint folder with nothing else set for it. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write the apply command as a shell script around psql, a Python script or a Makefile target; any of the three is acceptable. \\  \\ Apply every file in migrations/ in filename order, then load every data file in seed/. \\  \\ Pass -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 to psql, or a half-applied migration reports an error, carries on and exits zero. \\  \\ Fail the load rather than skipping a row that cannot be mapped, or a mapping bug becomes missing data nobody notices until Sprint 4 plots it. \\  \\ Copy the migration and seed loading into infra/postgres/ so that a fresh docker compose up -d builds the database unattended from Sprint 6. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A command that works only after three variables have been exported by hand fails the harness and will fail for your teammates too. \\ * Run it often. A schema that only works because of something a teammate typed into psql on Tuesday will not survive the showcase.

Summary: Load the Provided Seed Data
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * All of the provided seed data loads with one command, in full, with referential integrity intact. \\ * Accounts exist in all three states after loading, so the refusal paths in Sprint 6 are reachable. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Read seed/README.md, the data dictionary for the four provided files, before you design rather than after. \\  \\ Decide how many tables the data belongs in, which column becomes a key, and what identifies an account internally; the loading is where those decisions get tested. \\  \\ Map the customer-facing account reference the orders carry onto whatever identifies an account internally, which is the mapping the Trade REST API performs in Sprint 6. \\  \\ Load every row. Adding rows of your own is fine; removing rows is not. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The provided set covers accounts in all three states, an account with almost no cash, an instrument that no longer trades, orders in all four lifecycle states, and holdings that reconcile against the filled orders that produced them. \\ * Every one of those exists to make an error path reachable somewhere later in the programme.

Summary: The Six Named Queries and the Index Justifications
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The six named queries are written in SQL, run against the loaded data, and return sensible answers. \\ * At least three indexes exist and each is justified by one of the named queries, in design/indexes.md. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write the six queries from the brief and run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on each before and after adding an index. \\  \\ Justify three indexes against three of queries 1 to 5: name the query, state what the plan does with and without the index, and say what the index costs on write. \\  \\ Record any query that needs no new index because a key you already declared serves it, with the plan that proves it. \\  \\ Answer query 6 with a window function or a common table expression; it earns no index and is brought to the review. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * An index is paid for on every insert and every update to the columns it covers, and orders is the most write-heavy table you have. \\ * It seemed likely to help is not a justification.

Summary: Historical Trade Data Design (DESIGN.md)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * DESIGN.md covers what is retained about an executed trade beyond what the order carries, at what grain, how it is populated and by which component. \\ * It covers how the Sprint 7 extract pulls incrementally rather than scanning the whole history, how the design behaves at a hundred times the volume, and what it costs on write and in operational complexity. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write two pages in DESIGN.md covering retention grain, population, incremental extraction, growth and cost. \\  \\ State a position on partitioning, archival and retention, or make a defensible argument that none of it is needed yet. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Reduced for this cohort to a documented design rather than a built implementation. It is discussed at the design review, and a decision you can defend beats a diagram nobody can explain.

Summary: Harness Manifest and Probe Statements
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * manifest.env declares the apply command and the handful of names the harness needs, and the harness passes against your schema. \\ * Both probe statements are written and behave as the harness expects. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Fill in manifest.env once the first migration exists: the apply command, the accounts table, its state column and the three literal values it stores, the orders table and the column carrying the idempotency key. \\  \\ Write probes/duplicate-idempotency-key.sql to insert one valid order twice with the same key; the harness expects the second insert to fail with SQLSTATE 23505. \\  \\ Write probes/orphan-foreign-key.sql to insert one row referencing a parent that does not exist; the harness expects SQLSTATE 23503. \\  \\ Run sprint-03-trade-database/scripts/check.sh until it is green. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The harness never asserts a name it was not given, and it has no opinion about the rest of your schema. \\ * Passing is necessary and not sufficient. It cannot tell you whether the schema is in third normal form or whether an index is justified rather than merely present.

Summary: Analytics & Ingestion Pipeline (Python)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Three or more business claims, each supported by a chart a non-technical reader can read unaided. \\ * Ingestion is separated into extract, transform and load functions, in three modules of one installable Python project. \\ * Fauxnance candles are pulled through GET /candles/{symbol} with the key read from the environment, and pytest covers at least the transform including one malformed-input case. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * No project skeleton ships with this sprint. The team sets one up; the fixtures, the malformed payload and the acceptance harness are provided. \\ * The symbol universe must include at least two NSE or BSE instruments so that the cohort analyses a market it knows. \\ * The test suite never touches the network. fixtures/ holds three canned responses in the real envelope shape, one of them deliberately corrupted. \\ * Sprint 7 extends this project rather than replacing it, so choose libraries you are willing to live with for the rest of the programme. \\ * Definition of done includes sprint-04-analytics-etl/scripts/check.sh passing. \\ * Security focus: validation and data quality checks (OWASP A08), and a key that is read from the environment and never reaches the repository.

Summary: Python Project and the Engineering Contract
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * pip install -e sprint-04-analytics-etl works from the repository root on a machine that has never seen your code. \\ * The project declares a dev optional dependency group that brings pytest, and pytest run from the folder finds the suite in tests/. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Set up the packaging metadata, choosing the package name, module names, build backend and dependency set yourself. \\  \\ Declare the package, the three pipeline functions and the malformed-input test in manifest.env so the harness adapts to your names. \\  \\ Give the pipeline an entry point a teammate can run without reading the source, and say which in a note at the bottom of claims.md.

Summary: Fauxnance Client, Key Handling and Caching
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Candles are pulled through GET /candles/{symbol} with the key sent in the X-Api-Key header and read from FAUXNANCE_API_KEY. \\ * Raw responses are cached to disk keyed by symbol and range, so that re-running the pipeline costs nothing against the quota. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Read the key from the environment only. It is never a literal in source, a test, a fixture or a committed notebook. \\  \\ Cache the raw response rather than the cleaned frame, because changing the transform is what you will do most this week. \\  \\ Check GET /usage before assuming the API is broken, and GET /health, which needs no key, before assuming anything at all. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The quota is 2000 requests per day per key. A year of daily candles for one symbol is one request, so a team that runs out this week has a pull inside a loop that should have been a cache lookup. \\ * A key that reaches a commit has to be revoked, and the history keeps it whether or not you revoke it.

Summary: Symbol Universe including NSE or BSE Instruments
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The symbols in scope include at least two NSE or BSE instruments. \\ * The universe is small enough to produce three claims you can stand behind in the time available. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Choose the symbol universe and record it with the reason for each entry. \\  \\ Include Indian symbols such as INFY.NS, RELIANCE.NS or TATASTEEL.BO, all of which price through Fauxnance. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A chart is easier to sanity-check when you already know roughly what the numbers should look like, and a claim about a market you follow is easier to defend in the review.

Summary: Extract, Transform and Load as Three Modules
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Extract, transform and load are importable callables living in three distinct modules, wired together by a fourth that does nothing else. \\ * Transform opens no socket, reads no environment variable and writes nowhere; load is the only part that writes. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write extract to obtain raw responses and hand them on unchanged; it is the only part that needs a key and a network. \\  \\ Write transform to take data and return data: parsing, typing, cleaning, aggregating, deriving. \\  \\ Write load to write the result into the analytical store. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The split earns its keep the first time a number comes out wrong. One function that fetches, cleans and writes gives you no way to ask which third of it was wrong.

Summary: Error Handling for the Four Failure Modes
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Rate-limit and error handling are present and tell the four failure modes apart; a bare try around the whole run does not meet the criterion. \\ * A log line lets a teammate tell which of the four happened without rerunning the pipeline, and the key never appears in a log. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ On 429, stop and say so plainly, reading Retry-After; sleeping until midnight inside a batch run is not recovery. \\  \\ On another 4xx, fail that symbol, keep the message and carry on with the others; retrying repeats the mistake. \\  \\ On a connection error or timeout, retry with a growing backoff and give up after a small number of attempts. \\  \\ On a 200 carrying a bad payload, hand the decision to the transform: dropping, quarantining and raising are all defensible.

Summary: Transform Tests against the Provided Fixtures
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * pytest covers at least the transform, including one malformed-input case, and the suite never touches the network. \\ * The malformed-input test is declared in manifest.env as a pytest node id and passes when run on its own. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Read the canned responses from fixtures/ from disk, or wrap them in a pytest fixture of your own. \\  \\ Read fixtures/README.md, decide what your transform does with each of the six defects in the malformed payload, then assert it. \\  \\ Write the transform tests as you write the transform, not on the last evening. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid input transforms to expected output \\ # missing required field is rejected \\ # out-of-range value is flagged \\ # a high below its low is not loaded \\ # empty dataset handled without error \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Dropping a row, quarantining it and raising are not equally defensible for all six defects. What is not defensible is loading a row that says a share traded at a high below its low and then drawing a chart from it.

Summary: Three Business Claims and the Charts that Support Them
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Three or more insights are stated as business claims in claims.md, each naming the chart artefact that supports it. \\ * Each chart has both axes labelled with units, a title that states the finding, and no unexplained abbreviation or ticker without a company name. \\ * The chart artefacts open with no network and no build step. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write each claim as a sentence about the business that could turn out to be wrong: what is true, of what, over what period, and by how much. \\  \\ Compute candidates such as traded volume by date, exposure by instrument and average trade size over a period. \\  \\ Commit one artefact per claim, or one file holding all three charts, and point at a chart inside a combined file with a fragment. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A chart description is not a claim. It tells the reader what the picture is of and leaves them to work out whether anything follows. \\ * The reader has your chart and no access to you.

Summary: Define and Load the Analytical Store
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The dimensional model in contracts/analytics-schema.sql is created in the analytical store and the prepared data loads into it. \\ * The star schema and its grain are documented. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create DIM_ACCOUNT, DIM_INSTRUMENT, DIM_DATE and FACT_TRADES from the provided schema. \\  \\ Load dimensions before facts, because a fact row referencing a key that does not exist yet fails for a reason that reads like something else. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * contracts/analytics-schema.sql is plain ANSI SQL and runs unchanged on Snowflake, DuckDB or SQLite. DuckDB is the recommended default where no Snowflake account has been issued, and neither fallback costs marks: the model and the load are what is assessed. \\ * This schema is the load target for the Sprint 7 batch load.

Summary: Trading Domain Engine (Java & OOAD)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The trading domain engine is built in Java 21: four entities, three enumerations, the order request DTO, an exception hierarchy covering six cases, and business rules 1 to 8. \\ * The rules live in the domain and not in a caller, and no database, HTTP or Spring dependency reaches the module. \\ * Tests are written before implementation, evidenced in commit history, and the three named test classes are green. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * There are no stubs and no project skeleton. Designing these types from the requirements is the assessment. \\ * Core Java is a refresher for this cohort. What is assessed is the design, the evaluation order, the diagrams and the test-first discipline. \\ * Transport changes twice in the next fortnight: Sprint 6 calls these rules from a controller and Sprint 7 calls them from a Kafka consumer, which is why they live in a plain Java library neither caller can bend. \\ * Definition of done includes sprint-05-domain-engine/scripts/check.sh passing. \\ * Security focus: validation in the domain model, defensive coding, and an error message that leaks no internal detail (OWASP A05).

Summary: Maven Project and the Dependency Ban
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * One Maven project rooted in the sprint folder builds with mvn clean test-compile on a machine that has never seen your code. \\ * jakarta.validation-api is the only non-test dependency; Spring, a servlet API, a JDBC driver, MyBatis and a connection pool are absent from the dependency tree, including transitively. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Set up the project on Java 21 with JUnit 5 and surefire, sources under src/main/java and tests under src/test/java, below one base package declared in manifest.env. \\  \\ Ban the forbidden dependencies in your own build with the enforcer plugin's bannedDependencies rule, so a failing build tells whoever added one why. \\  \\ Run mvn install so that Sprint 6 can resolve this module from your local Maven repository by the coordinates you chose. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Bean Validation annotations are declarations rather than behaviour, which is why they are the one framework the architecture allows inside the domain.

Summary: Domain Modelling (UML Class and Sequence Diagrams)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A class diagram in design/ shows every type you wrote, its fields, the operations that carry behaviour, the enumerations, the exception hierarchy and the relationships with their cardinality. \\ * A sequence diagram shows one order arriving at the domain and the eight rules being evaluated in order, including where each failure leaves the flow. \\ * Both diagrams match the code and are walked in both directions at the review. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Draw the class diagram of your design, not of the model the brief describes. \\  \\ Draw the refusal paths on the sequence diagram; an order sailing through eight boxes and coming out accepted has not documented the interesting half. \\  \\ Commit Mermaid in design/class-diagram.md and design/sequence-diagram.md, or commit an exported image rather than a link to a cloud document. \\  \\ Update the diagrams when the code moves.

Summary: Domain Entities
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Account, Instrument, Order and Position are implemented and match the domain model. \\ * A debit that would leave the balance negative is refused before anything is subtracted, and money is decimal at two places rather than a double. \\ * A position never goes negative and an order reaches exactly one terminal state, with a disallowed transition refused by the order itself. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Give Account the cash balance, the holder, the trading status and the only operations that move that balance, plus the answer to whether it can afford an amount. \\  \\ Carry both account identifiers and keep them distinct: the numeric key is what accountId means everywhere in the API and in the JWT claim, and the string reference is what a support call quotes. \\  \\ Have the account report the version it was loaded at; the domain does not take the lock. \\  \\ Give Instrument the symbol in the Fauxnance scheme, the display name, the asset class, the currency of quotation and the answer to whether it may be traded. \\  \\ Make delisting a flag rather than a deleted row, because the order history references the symbol and that history is the audit trail. \\  \\ Implement the asymmetric average cost rule: a buy recalculates the average across the old holding and the new units, a sell reduces the quantity and leaves the average alone. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The limit price is what the customer submitted. The executed price is what the Trade Executor achieves against a live quote in Sprint 7 and does not exist until the order is filled.

Summary: Domain Enumerations
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * AccountStatus, OrderSide and OrderStatus each hold exactly the contractual literals, no more and no fewer. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create AccountStatus with ACTIVE, SUSPENDED and CLOSED. \\  \\ Create OrderSide with BUY and SELL. \\  \\ Create OrderStatus with NEW, FILLED, REJECTED and CANCELLED, spelling CANCELLED with two Ls. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * These appear in contracts/trade-api.yaml, the database stores the same strings, and Sprint 9 generates its types from that file, so a renamed or extra literal breaks three places at once. \\ * There is no partial-fill literal, which is why the Trade Executor fills in full or rejects.

Summary: Order Request DTO with Validation
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The order request DTO carries the six fields and every constraint the contract fixes on them. \\ * Every constraint is enforced and tested, including the boundary either side of each limit. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Model the DTO on the PlaceOrderRequest schema in contracts/trade-api.yaml, which is binding. \\  \\ Constrain the account key, the symbol, the side, the quantity, the price and the idempotency key as the contract states. \\  \\ Validate by annotation or by hand; either is allowed, and what is assessed is that the constraints hold. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid request passes validation \\ # null required field is rejected \\ # non-positive quantity is rejected \\ # non-positive price is rejected \\ # a value one step either side of each limit behaves as specified \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * These are business constraints rather than transport constraints, which is why the DTO lives here and not in the Sprint 6 service.

Summary: Exception Hierarchy
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Six exception types cover the six specified cases, all descending from a single domain base type. \\ * The base type carries the catalogue code and not an HTTP status, and the message is the catalogue message and nothing else. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create one type each for account not found, account not active, instrument not found, insufficient funds, insufficient holdings and duplicate order. \\  \\ Put anything an investigation needs on a typed field of the exception, logged on the server, rather than in the message. \\  \\ Decide what happens when a quantity or a price is out of range, given that the list of six has no member for it, and be ready to say what happens when the caller is the Trade Executor replaying an order and never ran a validator. \\  \\ Declare your six exception class names in manifest.env. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * One code can mean two things and one case can carry two codes, and neither is an accident. Sprint 6 maps the code to an HTTP status in one place and Sprint 7 maps it to a rejection reason on a Kafka event. \\ * Leaking internal detail in an error body is OWASP A05.

Summary: Business Rules 1 to 8
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Business rules 1 to 8 are implemented in the domain rather than in a controller, enforced in the stated order, and the first failure wins. \\ * A request breaking two rules receives the code of the first: a suspended account holding no cash gets ACC-403 rather than ORD-400. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Enforce existence, then active status, then a tradable instrument, then quantity, then price, then affordability on a buy, then held quantity on a sell, then the idempotency key. \\  \\ Check quantity and price in the rules as well as on the DTO, because the domain has to hold for a caller that never ran a validator. \\  \\ Leave room for the two rules that carry no code this sprint: cash and position move together or neither moves, and every order is recorded, including a rejected one. \\  \\ Design a seam that makes the idempotency rule expressible and testable here without a database, since in Sprint 6 the authority is the unique constraint you built in Sprint 3. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # buy succeeds and updates cash and position \\ # buy rejected on insufficient funds \\ # sell rejected on insufficient holdings \\ # order rejected on an account that does not exist \\ # order rejected on an inactive account \\ # order rejected on an unknown or non-tradable instrument \\ # duplicate idempotency key rejected \\ # a request breaking two rules returns the code of the first \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Rules in a controller get reimplemented by the Trade Executor, the copies drift, and the first drift accepts an order the executor then refuses.

Summary: Test-First JUnit Suite
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * AccountTest, OrderLogicTest and PlaceOrderRequestValidationTest are all green, with at least 24 tests across the three. \\ * The commit history shows the test for a rule in an earlier commit than the code that satisfies it. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write AccountTest over status, debit, credit, affordability, the refusal to go negative, and money that does not drift over many operations. \\  \\ Write OrderLogicTest over each of the eight rules firing and not firing, plus the evaluation order itself. \\  \\ Write PlaceOrderRequestValidationTest over every DTO constraint, including the boundary either side of each limit. \\  \\ Commit in small pieces so the history can show the discipline. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A single unit test is one class, one method, one execution path; cover error paths as isolated tests. \\ * A history in which a rule and its test first appear together does not meet the criterion, and one commit at the end of the week holding the whole module fails it outright.

Summary: Trade REST API (Spring Boot)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * All six endpoints implement contracts/trade-api.yaml, including the error envelope and every code in the catalogue. \\ * Layering is enforced, MyBatis mappers use parameterised statements throughout, order placement is transactional, and optimistic locking is applied on the account version. \\ * A protected route rejects a missing or invalid token with AUTH-401, and the service builds and runs from a multi-stage Dockerfile. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * No starter code, no stubs and no project skeleton ship. Deciding what belongs in which layer is most of what this sprint assesses. \\ * contracts/trade-api.yaml is provided and is neither authored nor changed by the team; OpenAPI-first is assessed against the provided contract. \\ * services/auth-stub is a provided fixture. Nothing in it is assessed and nothing in it is modified. Sprint 8 replaces it with the real service. \\ * GitHub Copilot is introduced this sprint for this cohort. What it produces is assessed exactly as anything you typed, and a generated mapper that interpolates a symbol fails the harness under your name. Keep a short walkthrough note for generated code you keep. \\ * Definition of done includes sprint-06-trade-api/scripts/check.sh, and scripts/check.sh --live once the stack is up. \\ * Security focus: verification before any claim is read, Bean Validation on request DTOs, and no stack trace or internal detail in a response body (OWASP A01, A03, A05).

Summary: Spring Boot Project and the Engineering Contract
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * One Maven project rooted in the sprint folder builds with mvn clean verify on a machine that has never seen your code. \\ * The Sprint 5 module resolves from the local Maven repository by the coordinates declared in manifest.env, and JWT_SECRET is read from the environment and appears in no committed file. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Set the project up on Java 21 with Spring Boot 3.5.x, the web and validation starters, the MyBatis starter and the Postgres driver. \\  \\ Run mvn install in sprint-05-domain-engine before mvn verify here, and again every time the domain changes. \\  \\ Declare the base package, the controller sub-package and the mapper sub-package in manifest.env; the layering checks find them by name.

Summary: Implement the Provided Trade API Contract
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The six operations answer at the paths, verbs and status codes the contract fixes, with response bodies matching the contract schemas field for field. \\ * Every failure leaves as the error envelope and nothing else: no whitelabel page, no stack trace, no bare status with an empty body. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Read contracts/trade-api.yaml and map every operation onto a controller method. \\  \\ Return the error envelope on every failure path so that Sprint 9 keeps one error handler for the whole platform. \\  \\ Note that AccountResponse.accountId is the one place in the platform where that name means the string business reference rather than the numeric key. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The contract exists so that Sprint 9 can generate a typed client without reading your Java. It is the thing you build, not documentation of something you build.

Summary: Layered Controller, Service and Mapper Structure
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Controllers hold no SQL, open no transaction and carry no business rule, and import nothing from the mapper package, java.sql, javax.sql, MyBatis, Spring JDBC or a persistence API. \\ * The service takes no servlet type, request object or status code as a parameter, and the domain module carries no HTTP type. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Put controllers in one sub-package and mappers in another, and keep the service between them. \\  \\ Wire dependency injection between the layers. \\  \\ Check that the published Sprint 5 artefact on the compile classpath references no servlet, Spring or MyBatis type. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The Trade Executor in Sprint 7 has no HTTP request and needs the same rules unchanged, so a rule taking a request DTO has bound the rules to one caller.

Summary: MyBatis Mappers with Parameterised Statements
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Every value arriving from outside is bound as a JDBC bind parameter; the harness fails the build on any string interpolation in a mapper. \\ * Result sets map cleanly onto the domain and DTO objects. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Write the mappers in XML under src/main/resources/mapper/ or in annotations on the mapper interface; either style is acceptable. \\  \\ Bind the account key, the symbol, the status filter and the timestamps as parameters, never as text substituted into the statement. \\  \\ If a column name or sort direction genuinely cannot be a bind parameter, check it against a fixed list of permitted names first and declare it in the manifest allowlist with a comment saying what does that checking. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # order row inserted and retrievable \\ # account and positions read correctly \\ # mapper reports the affected row count rather than returning void \\ # mapper surfaces a constraint violation rather than swallowing it \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A symbol of AAPL' OR '1'='1 substituted into a statement becomes part of that statement, and the positions that come back are whichever account the attacker asked for. That is OWASP A03. \\ * An allowlist entry is a question the review asks.

Summary: Order Placement: One Transaction and Optimistic Locking
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Order placement is transactional, so cash and position move together or neither moves. \\ * The update names the version the account row held when it was read and increments it; zero rows affected is refused with ORD-409 rather than treated as success. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Annotate the order placement path with @Transactional and keep the transaction around the work that has to be atomic and no more. \\  \\ Read the version with the row and return the affected row count from the mapper, because a mapper returning void has thrown away the only evidence that anything happened. \\  \\ Make the cancel transition conditional on the state you expect, in one statement. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # place order commits cash and position together \\ # failed order rolls back with no partial write \\ # a concurrent update is detected and the second writer is refused \\ # cancelling a filled order returns ORD-409 \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Without the lock, two buys of 20,000 against a balance of 25,000 both read the row, both write the same figure back, and nothing reports it until somebody reconciles the cash the next morning.

Summary: Account and Portfolio Read Endpoints
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The account read endpoints expose account details, cash balance, positions and order history, shaped by the contract schemas. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement the read operations the contract defines and shape the responses through the DTOs. \\  \\ Answer ACC-404 for an unknown account and ACC-403 where the token does not reach the account. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # account, balance, positions and order history returned successfully \\ # unknown account returns ACC-404 \\ # an account the token does not reach returns ACC-403 \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Exercise the read flows through the real controller, service and MyBatis persistence against Postgres. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Balance and positions are exposed here on the account endpoints. There is no separate Sprint 6 portfolio service; the Sprint 10 extension is a distinct service that adds valuation and profit and loss.

Summary: Global Exception Handler and the Error Catalogue
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A @ControllerAdvice maps every domain exception to its documented code and HTTP status, with no stack trace or internal detail in the body. \\ * The message is written for a human reading a screen: no class name, no SQL fragment, no account key, no internal identifier. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Map ACC-404 to 404, ACC-403 to 403, INS-404 to 404, ORD-400 to 400, ORD-409 to 409, VAL-422 to 422 and AUTH-401 to 401. \\  \\ Log what an investigation needs on the server rather than returning it. \\  \\ Confirm that clients can branch on the code, since 404 and 409 each carry more than one code. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # account not found maps to ACC-404 with status 404 \\ # inactive account maps to ACC-403 with status 403 \\ # unknown instrument maps to INS-404 with status 404 \\ # insufficient funds maps to ORD-400 with status 400 \\ # reused idempotency key maps to ORD-409 with status 409 \\ # invalid input maps to VAL-422 with status 422

Summary: JWT Verification against the Provided Auth Stub
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Every route under the API prefix is answered for token validity once, before any controller runs. \\ * A missing header, a wrong scheme, an expired token and a forged signature all return AUTH-401 with the same body. \\ * A token that does not reach the addressed account returns ACC-403 with the same message a suspended account gets. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Check the signature, the expiry and the algorithm the token asks for, in that order, before reading a claim. \\  \\ Read the demo users, the claims and the shared signing secret from services/auth-stub/README.md; the stub starts with the infrastructure. \\  \\ Answer authorisation where the account key is known, not in the filter. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A verifier that decodes the payload first has already trusted whatever the client sent. \\ * A more specific message tells an attacker which of the four failures they got, and the identical ACC-403 message stops anyone enumerating account keys. \\ * Sprint 8 swaps the stub for the real service as a configuration change. If yours needs a code change, something is coupled to the stub rather than to the token, and that is worth finding now.

Summary: Multi-Stage Dockerfile and the Compose Entry
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The service builds and runs from a multi-stage Dockerfile whose final stage is not a build image and does not run as root. \\ * docker compose up -d --profile platform starts the service, which resolves postgres and the auth stub by service name and reports healthy. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the jar in a stage carrying Maven and a JDK, and take it into a stage carrying a Java runtime and neither of the other two. \\  \\ Order the copies so that changing a source file does not invalidate the resolved-dependency layer. \\  \\ Build both projects inside the image build, because it starts with an empty local Maven repository and cannot reach the Sprint 5 module on your laptop. \\  \\ Add the service to the root docker-compose.yml under the platform profile, on trading-net, with a published port, database and JWT_SECRET values from the environment, depends_on Postgres on its health condition, and a health check. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Every tool in an image is a tool available to whoever gets into the container, which is the reason to care rather than disk. \\ * Nothing this sprint needs Kafka.

Summary: Event Backbone (Kafka, Trade Executor & Batch Load)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Three topics are created with documented keys and partition counts, and the Trade REST API publishes to orders and returns NEW. \\ * The Trade Executor consumes, prices against a live Fauxnance quote, applies the fill or reject rule, updates order, cash and position in one transaction, and publishes to trade-events. \\ * Replaying a duplicate message does not double-debit an account and the team can demonstrate it; the poller batches up to 25 symbols and stays inside the quota; one incremental load reaches FACT_TRADES with dead-letter handling; the SonarQube gate passes. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * There is no Broker Simulator on this platform and there will not be one. The team builds the execution venue, and it is the only component that decides whether an order fills. \\ * Monday is Ganesh Chaturthi, so this is a four-taught-day week. Take the poller first, then the change to the Sprint 6 service with its characterisation tests committed ahead of it, then the executor, which is most of the week, then the batch load alongside the last day. \\ * No starter code and no project skeleton ship. Deciding how the executor is decomposed, and where the fill rule lives inside it, is most of what this sprint assesses. \\ * Characterisation tests are written around the team's own Sprint 6 code. This branch ships clean stubs and there is no planted starter codebase to refactor. \\ * The batch load is reduced for this cohort to a single incremental load into FACT_TRADES and its dimensions: no scheduler, no orchestration, no history rebuild and no reconciliation job. \\ * The Fauxnance key is read from the environment in both new services and is shared between them, so a poller that spends the whole allowance leaves the executor with nothing. \\ * Definition of done includes sprint-07-event-backbone/scripts/check.sh, and scripts/check.sh --live once the stack is up. \\ * Security focus: DevSecOps in CI with SAST, dependency scanning and secret detection, and the SonarQube quality gate (OWASP A06, A08).

Summary: Three Kafka Topics and the Message Envelope
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The orders, trade-events and market-data topics exist with the keys and partition counts contracts/kafka-topics.md fixes, alongside their dead-letter topics. \\ * Every message carries the five-field envelope, and the team can explain the key and partition decisions at the review. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Create orders and trade-events keyed by the account, and market-data keyed by the symbol, with the partition counts the contract fixes. \\  \\ Create the three dead-letter topics explicitly; auto-creation is off because it produces a one-partition topic with the wrong retention and nothing tells you it happened. \\  \\ Document why the key decides the partition and the partition decides the ordering, and why keying orders by order identifier would throw the guarantee away. \\  \\ Write consumers that ignore fields they do not recognise, since one that fails on an unknown field turns an additive change into an outage. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Partitions can be increased and never decreased, and increasing them rehashes the keys, so an account's history splits from that point onwards.

Summary: Characterisation Tests on Your Own Sprint 6 Code
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Characterisation tests pin the Sprint 6 order placement path and are committed before that service is changed. \\ * The first commit adding a file under the declared characterisation test directory is a proper ancestor of the first commit that changes the Sprint 6 sources. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Record what the service does now, including the parts you disagree with, rather than what you think it should do. \\  \\ Pin what comes back for an affordable order field by field including the status, and which code and status come back for a reused idempotency key, an unaffordable buy, an unknown symbol and an account that is not ACTIVE. \\  \\ Pin what is written to the order row, the cash and the position when an order is accepted. \\  \\ Keep them in one package of their own, named in CHARACTERISATION_TEST_DIR in manifest.env, and commit them before the change. \\  \\ Where the change deliberately alters a pinned behaviour, change that test in the same commit as the change and say so in the message. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * You cannot write one afterwards: a test written against changed code records the behaviour of the changed code, which is the one thing it cannot then be used to check. \\ * Tests and a change to the service in the same commit do not satisfy the criterion. Neither does a history where the service was changed first and pinned afterwards. \\ * Three tests is the floor the harness enforces, and it is a floor rather than a target.

Summary: Trade REST API Publishes ORDER_PLACED and Answers NEW
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * POST to the orders endpoint writes the order at NEW, answers NEW, and publishes ORDER_PLACED to the orders topic keyed by the account. \\ * The event is published after the transaction commits, not inside it. \\ * Nothing else about the service changes: validation, layering, the error catalogue, the optimistic lock and token verification all stay as they are. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Remove the synchronous fill from the endpoint; there is no price in that request and pricing is the executor's job. \\  \\ Configure the producer with acks=all, enable.idempotence=true, a high retry count and no more than five requests in flight per connection. \\  \\ Choose the recoverable failure: an order that committed and was never published can be replayed from the order table, and an event for an order that rolled back cannot be undone. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # an accepted order is written at NEW and answered NEW \\ # ORDER_PLACED is published for a newly accepted order \\ # the event is published only after the transaction has committed \\ # an order that fails validation publishes nothing \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * An idempotent producer removes the duplicates a producer retry causes, not the duplicates an application retry causes, which is why the executor still has work to do.

Summary: Trade Executor: Consume, Price and Decide
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The executor consumes ORDER_PLACED from orders in the fixed consumer group, loads the order, checks the instrument is still tradable, and prices it against a live Fauxnance quote. \\ * The fill rule is a function of an order and a quote returning a decision, touching no database and no socket. \\ * An order that cannot be priced is resolved rather than left at NEW for ever. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Set the project up as one Maven project on Java 21, with every instance joining the consumer group the contract fixes. \\  \\ Fetch a quote from the single-symbol quotes endpoint for the order symbol. \\  \\ Start from the default rule: fill the whole order at the quoted price when a BUY limit is at or above the quote or a SELL limit is at or below it, and reject otherwise. \\  \\ Settle four questions and be ready to defend each: what price is stored given the quote carries more decimal places than the column holds, which of the Sprint 5 rules are re-checked here, what a suspended account does when the suspension arrived after acceptance, and what happens when there is no price. \\  \\ Treat a Fauxnance outage as a business outcome: retry inside the quote client and reject the order with a reason when the budget is spent. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # a buy limit at or above the quote fills at the quote \\ # a sell limit at or below the quote fills at the quote \\ # an order outside the marketable range is rejected \\ # an execution-time re-check rejects an order whose account can no longer afford it \\ # an account suspended after acceptance does not trade \\ # an order with no available price is resolved rather than left at NEW \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Run the executor against a mocked quote source covering a fill, a reject and a pricing-unavailable response. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Partial fills are out of scope, because the order status enumeration has no state to represent one and there is no working state between NEW and a terminal status.

Summary: Settle in One Transaction with Two Guards
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The status change, the cash movement and the position write happen in one transaction; if any of the three fails, none of them happened. \\ * The guarded state transition is the first write in the transaction and is conditional on the order still being NEW, and zero rows affected means another delivery got there first. \\ * The event is published after the commit and the offset is acknowledged after the publish. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Make the status update conditional on the state you expect rather than reading, deciding, then writing. \\  \\ Apply the optimistic lock on the account version, re-reading and retrying up to a bounded number of attempts, and treat only an exhausted budget as an error. \\  \\ Publish ORDER_FILLED or ORDER_REJECTED to trade-events keyed by the account, then acknowledge. \\  \\ Add the columns the executor writes and your Sprint 3 schema may not have yet as a migration in the same folder and style as your Sprint 3 migrations. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # a settled order writes status, cash and position together \\ # a failure in any of the three leaves none of them written \\ # a second delivery affects zero rows and publishes nothing \\ # an exhausted optimistic-lock budget is reported as an error rather than ignored \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * An order marked filled beside cash that did not move leaves the audit trail disagreeing with the balance, and nothing reconciles the two for you. \\ * Publishing before the commit risks an event for a transaction that rolled back. Acknowledging before publishing risks an order that settled and told nobody.

Summary: Duplicate Delivery: Prove No Double Debit
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A replayed message does not debit the account twice and produces no second message on trade-events. \\ * The team can give the demonstration on demand, at any point in the review. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Read one message off the orders topic with the console consumer and produce it back with the console producer, preserving the key. \\  \\ Show the balance before, the balance after, the log line where the executor recognised the duplicate and did nothing, and that no second event appeared on trade-events. \\  \\ Rehearse it as a team; being able to run the harness is not the same as being able to give the demonstration. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This demonstration is mandatory for this cohort. \\ * Kafka guarantees at-least-once deliberately, because the alternative is a broker that occasionally loses a trade. The executor will be handed the same order twice. \\ * A consumer that believes the order happened twice is the same bug one service further downstream.

Summary: Executor Failure Handling and Dead Letters
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A message that will never succeed is dead-lettered on the first attempt, and one that will succeed later is retried with a growing backoff and dead-lettered once the budget is spent. \\ * No poison message is retried indefinitely. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Dead-letter malformed JSON, a missing order identifier, an order identifier that is not in Postgres and an unexpected event type immediately. \\  \\ Retry a briefly unreachable broker, a lost database connection and an exhausted lock budget with backoff. \\  \\ Send dead-lettered messages to the topic's dead-letter topic with the original message as the value and the failure reason in a header. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # a malformed message is dead-lettered on the first attempt \\ # a transient failure is retried and then succeeds \\ # a poison message does not block the partition \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * One bad message blocking a partition stops every account keyed to that partition. \\ * A Fauxnance outage belongs in neither class: dead-lettering the order would leave it at NEW for ever.

Summary: Market-Data Poller
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The poller calls the batch quotes endpoint on an interval, batching up to 25 symbols per request, and publishes one message per symbol to market-data keyed by the symbol. \\ * The configured interval stays inside the 2000-requests-per-day quota, and the arithmetic can be shown. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Set the poller up as one Python project, importable and installable, with its tests in the sprint folder and its test dependencies under a dev group. \\  \\ Publish one Kafka message per symbol, never one per batch: batching the HTTP call is a quota optimisation, and batching the Kafka message puts several symbols behind one key and destroys the per-symbol ordering the contract promises. \\  \\ Poll only the symbols someone holds or is watching, and enforce the interval floor in the code rather than documenting one and hoping. \\  \\ Work out the requests per day your interval implies and declare it in manifest.env. \\  \\ Join the poller to the compose stack under the platform profile with the broker address and the key from the environment. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # a batch of up to 25 symbols is fetched in one request \\ # each quote is published as its own message keyed by symbol \\ # the configured interval stays inside the daily quota for the declared symbol set \\ # the interval floor is enforced in code \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The poller is what manufactures the stream Fauxnance does not have, and its existence is the reason the Sprint 10 extensions that read prices have anything to consume. \\ * Eight symbols fetched one at a time every 30 seconds is 23040 requests and the key is gone in two hours; the same data batched is 2880.

Summary: One Incremental Load into FACT_TRADES
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * One incremental load moves trade data from Postgres into FACT_TRADES and its three dimensions, driven by a watermark on the order creation timestamp. \\ * Re-running a load does not double-count, and a row failing a quality check is dead-lettered with the reason and the batch it came from rather than dropped. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Load dim_date first, covering the whole range, then dim_instrument, then dim_account, then fact_trades. \\  \\ Load orders in whatever status they reached, including rejected and cancelled, because fill rate cannot be computed from fills alone. \\  \\ Merge on the natural order key rather than inserting blindly, and rely on the unique constraint the contract declares. \\  \\ Run every check the contract's load and data quality section names before a row reaches the fact table: referential integrity into all three dimensions, positive quantity and price, a valid side and status, and a recomputed trade value. \\  \\ Declare the three pipeline commands in manifest.env. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # an incremental load populates FACT_TRADES \\ # a second load with no new data adds no rows \\ # the transform handles nulls and type mismatches \\ # an invalid row is dead-lettered with its reason and the load continues \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Do not insert a placeholder dimension row to make an unresolved key pass: that hides the fault, which is almost always that the dimension load was skipped. \\ * Dropping a row silently and dead-lettering it produce the same fact table, and only one of them can be investigated on Monday morning.

Summary: SonarQube Quality Gate and DevSecOps Scanning
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The SonarQube gate passes on the Java service and on the pipeline: no new blocker or critical issue, no new security hotspot left unreviewed, duplication and coverage on new code inside the thresholds. \\ * SAST, dependency scanning and secret detection run locally against the same code, and anything they report is fixed rather than left for the review. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Run SonarQube locally in a container named for your team, and scan both the executor and the pipeline. \\  \\ Export the scanner token rather than committing it; it is a credential. \\  \\ Run the analysis and the security scans locally, and interpret the findings rather than silencing them. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Passing by marking findings as will not fix is visible in the dashboard and is not passing. \\ * The harness does not run SonarQube, so the gate is read at the review, on your screen, on the project you scanned.

Summary: Authentication Service (NestJS & JWT)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * All four endpoints implement contracts/auth-api.yaml, and the access token carries exactly the contract claim set. \\ * Passwords are hashed with argon2id or bcrypt at cost 12 or above and never logged, and a failed login gives the same response and comparable timing for an unknown user as for a wrong password. \\ * Swapping the stub for this service is a configuration change only with no Java changed in the Trade REST API, the running service serves its own OpenAPI document, and the security review is committed with a finding and a disposition for every category. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This is the one component that ever sees a credential. Every other component verifies a signature with no network call and no shared database. \\ * No starter code and no project skeleton ship. Deciding how the service is decomposed, and where the verification happens inside it, is most of what the sprint assesses. \\ * Two SME cloud sessions run on Monday and Tuesday, so the build has three days. Take registration and login first, then the guard and the protected route, then refresh, then the cutover, filling in the security review as each part lands. \\ * Refresh rotation is reduced for this cohort to issuing a new refresh token on every refresh. Revoking the presented token is optional; where it is not built, the decision and the risk it accepts are written in the security review and declared in manifest.env. \\ * Definition of done includes sprint-08-auth-service/scripts/check.sh, and scripts/check.sh --live once the stack is up. \\ * Security focus: password storage, the token lifecycle, uniform failure, and defence against leakage and replay (OWASP A02, A07, A01).

Summary: NestJS Project and the Engineering Contract
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * npm ci, npm run build and npm test all succeed on a machine that has never seen your code, from a committed lock file. \\ * The service answers on the port the contract fixes, builds from a multi-stage Dockerfile, and joins the root compose file in place of the auth stub. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Set the project up on Node 20 or later in TypeScript, with sources under the directory declared in manifest.env and specs beside the code they cover. \\  \\ Read JWT_SECRET, the database connection and every value that differs between a laptop and a container from the environment at runtime. \\  \\ Write the Dockerfile and the compose entry, removing the auth-stub service.

Summary: Implement the Provided Auth Contract
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The four operations answer at the paths, verbs, status codes and bodies contracts/auth-api.yaml fixes, with the documented failures. \\ * Every failure leaves in the platform envelope and nothing else. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement registration, login, refresh and the protected profile route against the contract. \\  \\ Issue no tokens on registration; an unauthenticated route that mints a session is an authentication bypass as soon as it has its first defect. \\  \\ Create no trading account on registration; accounts are owned by the Sprint 3 schema. \\  \\ Validate inputs with class-validator and class-transformer and answer VAL-422 on a field failure.

Summary: Credential Store and Password Hashing
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Passwords are stored with argon2id, or bcrypt at cost 12 or above, and plaintext is never stored. \\ * No password reaches a log by a direct route, and the cost factor is a decision the team can defend. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the credential store as a migration or bootstrap, plus the repository that reads it. \\  \\ Choose cost parameters that make one verification take on the order of a tenth of a second on the hardware you deploy to, and say why. \\  \\ Log through one logger that redacts by key name at any depth, and never hand a whole request body to a log call. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # correct password verifies \\ # incorrect password fails verification \\ # a general-purpose digest such as MD5 or SHA is not used \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A general-purpose hash is built to be fast, and fast is the one property a password hash must not have. \\ * Too low a cost gives an offline attacker the same speedup you got; too high and your login route is the cheapest denial-of-service target in the platform. \\ * The indirect routes to a log, such as an error object serialised whole or a DTO printed in a stack trace, are what the review asks about.

Summary: Access Token Issuance and the Exact Claim Set
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The access token is signed HS256 with JWT_SECRET and carries exactly the claim set the contract fixes, plus the issuer the contract defines. \\ * Anything outside that set is a finding, not a bonus, and expiry is set as the contract states. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build and sign the token, setting the issued-at and expiry claims as the contract requires. \\  \\ Carry the numeric trading account key in the account claim, which is what the Trade REST API compares against the account in the request. \\  \\ Set your own issuer value so that a team can decode a token during the cutover and see which implementation signed it, and do not require a particular issuer value in any consumer. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # a token is issued with the contract claims and expiry \\ # the token signature verifies with the service key \\ # no claim outside the contract set is present \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The payload is base64 and not encryption. An email address in the payload is an email address published to every holder of the token. \\ * Removing a claim after Sprint 9 has generated a client from it is not a configuration change.

Summary: Guard and Token Verification on the Protected Route
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The protected route is guarded, and an expired, tampered or malformed token is refused with AUTH-401. \\ * Jest covers the guard, including a passing test for the expired-token path and one for the wrong-signature path. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement the guard and a decorator that extracts the authenticated user from the verified token. \\  \\ Build the expired case by signing a genuine token with a past expiry, not by corrupting the payload, which the signature check refuses first. \\  \\ Build the wrong-signature case by signing a genuine, unexpired token with a different key. \\  \\ Name the specs so that the patterns declared in manifest.env reach them. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # a valid token is accepted \\ # an expired token is refused \\ # a token with a wrong signature is refused before any claim is read \\ # a malformed header is refused \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * A guard that checks the signature and forgets the clock accepts every token it ever issued, for ever.

Summary: Refresh Token Issuance and Rotation
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Every refresh issues a new refresh token and the new one works. \\ * Where revocation of the presented token is built, a second presentation answers AUTH-401; where it is not, the decision and its residual risk are written in the security review. \\ * The declared rotation behaviour in manifest.env matches what was built. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Store a hash of the refresh token rather than the token, so that read access to your database is not session takeover. \\  \\ Issue a new refresh token on every refresh. \\  \\ Decide whether to revoke the presented token, build it or document it, and declare the choice in manifest.env. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token \\ # the newly issued refresh token works \\ # the declared revocation behaviour holds for a token that has already been exchanged \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Reissue alone defends against a stolen token used once. What is missing without revocation is that the old value still works, so both parties hold live sessions and nothing in the service can tell there are two of them.

Summary: One Answer for Every Failed Login
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * An unknown username and a wrong password return the same status, the same body and comparable timing. \\ * A login throttle exists and is declared, and neither path returns early. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Return AUTH-401 with one message for an unknown user, a wrong password, an expired token, a wrongly signed token and a malformed header. \\  \\ Where the username is not found, verify the supplied password against a fixed dummy hash of the same algorithm and parameters, discard the result and return the same failure. \\  \\ Build the login throttle and declare its cooldown and the attempt count in manifest.env. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # an unknown user and a wrong password return the same status and body \\ # neither path returns before doing comparable work \\ # the throttle limits repeated failed attempts from one caller \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * An attacker with a username list and a stopwatch reads your customer base off the response times without guessing a password. \\ * A throttle limits how fast an attacker can use an oracle you left open. It does not close it.

Summary: Retire the Stub with a Configuration Change Only
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * At least one Trade REST API route is protected end to end by a token from this service, with no Java changed in that service. \\ * A token signed with a key the platform should not trust is refused. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Replace the auth-stub service in the root compose file with yours, on the same port. \\  \\ Read the same JWT_SECRET the Trade REST API verifies with, passed through compose from the root environment file. \\  \\ Point the Trade REST API's issuer setting at your issuer through its environment, if it pins one. \\  \\ Decide whether to keep or rotate the stub's published development secret now that the stub is gone, and declare the choice in manifest.env. \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Obtain a token from the running Auth service, call a protected Trade REST API route with it, and confirm refusal with no token and with a token signed by a key the platform should not trust. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The criterion is read with git diff at the design review; no script can tell a configuration change from a code change that looks like one. \\ * If your Trade REST API needs a code change, something in it is coupled to the fixture rather than to the token: a hard-coded issuer, a claim read with a name the stub happened to use, or a verifier that decoded before it verified.

Summary: OpenAPI Served by the Running Service
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The running service publishes its own OpenAPI document, generated from the decorators on the controller and the DTOs, describing the four routes. \\ * The human page and the JSON document answer at the paths declared in manifest.env. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Generate the document from your code rather than maintaining a YAML file by hand beside it. \\  \\ Declare both paths in manifest.env. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * This does not replace contracts/auth-api.yaml. It is the evidence that your code still matches it.

Summary: OWASP Security Review, Committed
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The security review is committed, differs from the template, and carries a written finding and a disposition for every category. \\ * A finding of none names what was checked, and a disposition of accepted states the residual risk and why the team is carrying it. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Copy security-review/TEMPLATE.md, name your copy in manifest.env, and fill it in as you build rather than on the last evening. \\  \\ Cover broken authentication and broken access control, token leakage, replay and weak secrets. \\  \\ Where revocation of the presented refresh token was not built, write that decision and its risk into the review. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The harness checks that the cells are filled. Whether what is in them is true is read by your instructor.

Summary: Trading UI (Angular)
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Sign-in works end to end against the real Auth service, route guards block unauthenticated access and redirect, and one interceptor attaches the bearer token to platform calls and to nothing else. \\ * Typed clients are generated from contracts/ and committed, the order ticket validates before submission and renders every code in both catalogues, and the blotter badges four statuses and handles an order sitting at NEW. \\ * Playwright covers signing in and placing an order, each journey standing on its own, and no API key and no secret is present in the built bundle. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * No workspace scaffold and no starter code ship. Setting the workspace up and deciding where each rule lives is most of what this sprint assesses. \\ * Angular 21 with standalone components and signals throughout. No NgModule anywhere, and the observables stop at HttpClient. \\ * Self-directed SRE content runs on Monday and Friday is Gandhi Jayanti, so this sprint runs to four taught days and the first is not spent in this folder. Stand the workspace up and generate the clients first, then sign-in, then the order ticket, then the blotter, and configure Playwright as soon as sign-in works. \\ * The Playwright suite is reduced for this cohort to the sign-in and place-order journeys. A third journey over the blotter is optional and declared in manifest.env. \\ * Execution has been asynchronous since Sprint 7. An order answering NEW is normal and is not a defect in the executor. \\ * Definition of done includes sprint-09-trading-ui/scripts/check.sh, and scripts/check.sh --live once the stack is up. \\ * Security focus: bearer token scoping by origin, an allow list rather than a deny list, and nothing secret in a public bundle (OWASP A01, A03, A05).

Summary: Angular Workspace and the Engineering Contract
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * npm ci, npm run build and npm test all succeed on a machine that has never seen your code, from a committed lock file. \\ * The workspace uses standalone components and signals, with specs beside the code they cover. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Set one Angular 21 workspace up in the sprint folder on a supported Node version. \\  \\ Decide the feature tree yourself and declare every path the harness reads in manifest.env.

Summary: Typed Clients Generated from the Contracts
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Clients for both contracts are generated rather than hand-written, with the generator and its version pinned in the declared configuration. \\ * The generated output is committed, regenerated on every contract change, and contains no file the generator did not write. \\ * Something outside the generated tree imports the clients. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Declare one entry per contract, each writing into its own subdirectory of the generated tree. \\  \\ Pin the generator version rather than taking whatever resolves today, so two people on the team generate the same output. \\  \\ Document the generation command in a README of your own in this folder. \\  \\ Commit the output, say so in .gitignore, and never edit a file inside the tree; wrap an awkward generated shape in a service of your own outside it. \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * When a contract changes a field, a generated client stops compiling at every call site that used it and a hand-written one keeps compiling and starts returning undefined at runtime. That is the whole reason the contract exists. \\ * The contracts are correct and are not yours to edit, so switch a generator validation off knowingly rather than reflexively.

Summary: Sign-In Flow against the Real Auth Service
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * A customer signs in against the running Auth service, the token is stored, and a failed sign-in shows a readable error. \\ * Signing out clears the session. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the sign-in screen with username and password inputs and a submit control. \\  \\ Give the username field, the password field and the submit control stable test identifiers; the harness drives that form with the selectors in manifest.env. \\  \\ Store the token and clear it on sign-out. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # valid credentials sign in and redirect \\ # invalid credentials show a readable error \\ # empty fields are blocked by validation \\ # signing out clears the session \\  \\ *Integration Test* \\  \\ Sign in against the real Auth service end to end.

Summary: The Bearer Token Interceptor
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * One functional interceptor, registered once, is the only place in the application that sets an authorisation header. \\ * The token is attached to platform API calls and to nothing else, decided by comparing the outgoing URL against the origins you configured. \\ * Two named unit tests cover the attach case and the do-not-attach case. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Register the interceptor once rather than setting the header in each service. \\  \\ Attach the token to the Trade REST API and the protected Auth route, and not to the unauthenticated auth routes, which take no header. \\  \\ Use an allow list of origins rather than a deny list of hosts you happened to think of. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # a request to a platform API carries the bearer token \\ # a request to a third-party origin does not carry the bearer token \\ # the unauthenticated auth routes are called without a header \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * An interceptor that adds the header to every outbound request hands a live session token to whatever host that request was going to, where it lands in an access log, an analytics pipeline and an error tracker. \\ * An allow list fails closed when somebody adds a new third party. A deny list fails open, silently.

Summary: Route Guards and the Return Address
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Every route but sign-in runs a guard, and a signed-out visitor is redirected to sign-in carrying where they were going. \\ * A return address is accepted only if it is a path on this origin. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Implement the guard and the redirect, and land the user where they were going after signing in. \\  \\ Reject a return address that is not a path on this origin. \\  \\ Do not render an empty screen instead of redirecting; a user who has been told nothing will retry, then raise a ticket. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # the guard blocks unauthenticated navigation and redirects \\ # the guard allows authenticated navigation \\ # an off-origin return address is refused \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * The guard is a usability control, not a security control. The bundle is public and authorisation is the Trade REST API's decision, taken on every call. \\ * An open redirect on a trading sign-in page is a phishing kit somebody else assembles for free.

Summary: Order Ticket with Client-Side Validation
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * The order ticket validates quantity, price and symbol before submission and renders the account read-only. \\ * A submitted order shows the outcome the API returned, including an order that comes back at NEW. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Build the ticket with instrument, side, quantity and price inputs, validating a whole quantity above zero and a price above zero with at most two decimal places. \\  \\ Render the account the token says this session may trade as read-only, because an account field the user can edit is an authorisation decision moved into the browser. \\  \\ Show a success or error message from the response. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # a valid order submits and shows the returned status \\ # an invalid quantity is blocked before submission \\ # a business-rule rejection shows the mapped message \\  \\ *Notes:* \\  \\ * Client-side validation is not enforcement. The business rules live in the Trade REST API and stay there; the form exists so that the obvious mistakes never reach the wire.

Summary: Render Every Code in the Error Catalogues
Description: *Acceptance Criteria:* \\  \\ * Every error code in both contracts renders as a readable message, and the application branches on the code rather than on the message. \\ * A response the browser never received and a code the application has never seen both render a sentence rather than a blank panel. \\  \\ *Tasks:* \\  \\ Read the codes out of the two contracts and build the mapping as a mapping with a completeness property, not a switch statement extended when somebody reports a blank screen. \\  \\ Write sentences a trader can act on rather than repeating the developer-facing message. \\  \\ Handle a status of zero, which is usually a service that is down or a cross-origin rule that does not allow your development server. \\  \\ *Unit Test Execution Paths:* \\  \\ # every code in both catalogues maps to a message \\ # an unrecognised code falls back to a readable sentence \\ # a request that never reached a service renders a readable sentence

Summary: Blotter with Status Badges and the NEW Path
